stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Jun 2026 case surge
frames.note: Story begins this month as confirmed cases climb past 676 to 782 with 181 deaths, two new health zones report infections, and World Cup host cities ready contingency screening. Under this frame the situation reads as a fast-moving cross-border threat measured day by day. This is the frame US outlets, FIFA-adjacent coverage, and wire-service desks open with.

frames.label: May 2026 PHEIC
frames.note: Story begins with the WHO declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern roughly a month before today and the response that followed. Under this frame events read as the unfolding of a declared emergency where coordination gaps and community distrust define the arc. This is the frame MSF, WHO Africa, and global-health reporters open with.

frames.label: 2018 Kivu epidemic
frames.note: Story begins with the 2018 to 2020 North Kivu and Ituri outbreak and the vaccine programs and armed-conflict pressures that shaped it. Under this frame the current surge reads as the latest cycle in eastern DRC's recurring pattern of outbreak plus conflict. This is the frame epidemiologists and longtime DRC correspondents open with.

frames.label: 1976 Yambuku
frames.note: Story begins at the original 1976 identification of Ebola near the Ebola River in northern Zaire and the half-century of flare-ups since. Under this frame each new outbreak reads as continuous with a long regional history and with debates over dependence on outside aid. This is the frame Pan-African commentators and Countercurrents-style sovereignty voices open with.

bands.label: Case surge and World Cup watch
bands.summary: Cases climb from 676 past 782 with 181 deaths, two new health zones report infections, Kenya disputes a Laikipia facility build, and World Cup host cities prepare contingency screening.

nodes.title: Confirmed case count reaches 710 with 149 deaths
nodes.what: Health authorities report the running tally of laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases climbing to 710 in eastern Congo, with 149 reported deaths. The figures cover the period before the latest weekly update and frame the trajectory of the outbreak heading into mid June.

nodes.title: Cases reach 782 and deaths 181 as two new health zones report infections
nodes.what: DR Congo health officials announce that confirmed cases have climbed to 782 with 181 reported deaths. Two additional health zones in the east are added to the list of areas reporting infections, broadening the geographic footprint of the outbreak.

nodes.title: MSF warns of dangerous gaps one month into response
nodes.what: Medecins Sans Frontieres releases a one-month review of the Ebola response in DR Congo, warning of persistent dangerous gaps in case finding, treatment capacity, and community engagement. Samaritan's Purse is also reported setting up treatment centers in the outbreak zone alongside other responders.

nodes.title: Dispute over Laikipia Air Base Ebola facility in Kenya
nodes.what: Kenyan opposition figure Rigathi Gachagua publicly demands media access to Laikipia Air Base over a disputed Ebola facility construction project. Demonstrations against the facility take place and reports emerge of police shooting protesters, drawing the regional response into a domestic political confrontation.
nodes.disputed: AllAfrica describes the events as Gachagua demanding transparency over a disputed facility construction; the World Socialist Web Site describes the same period as police killing three at anti-Ebola facility demonstrations.

nodes.title: DR Congo squad arrives in Houston for World Cup after 21 day isolation
nodes.what: The DR Congo national football team arrives in Houston for the 2026 World Cup after completing a 21 day isolation period tied to the outbreak. Coverage frames the arrival as a marker of how the public health timeline now overlaps with the tournament schedule.

nodes.title: World Cup host cities ready contingency screening
nodes.what: US World Cup host cities outline contingency screening and health protocols ahead of tournament matches. Public health experts quoted in coverage describe the imported case risk for the tournament as extremely low while emphasizing that US hospitals and federal agencies are prepared.

nodes.title: Fear grips Bunia as Ituri businesses lose income
nodes.what: Reporting from Bunia in Ituri province describes daily life slowing as residents avoid public gatherings and markets and traders report sharp income losses. The pattern echoes earlier outbreak responses in the region and adds an economic dimension to the public health emergency.

bands.label: PHEIC and early response
bands.summary: WHO declares a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, MSF and Samaritan's Purse set up treatment centers, and responders warn of dangerous gaps and growing distrust.

nodes.title: WHO declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern
nodes.what: After an emergency committee meeting, the World Health Organization classified the rising Ebola caseload in DR Congo as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The designation unlocked international coordination mechanisms, financing channels, and reporting obligations for member states. WHO Director-General framed the declaration as a step needed to align cross-border surveillance and logistics.

nodes.title: Samaritan's Purse opens treatment center
nodes.what: Samaritan's Purse, the US-based Christian relief organization, opened an Ebola treatment center in coordination with Congolese health authorities. The charity flew in clinicians, modular ward equipment, and personal protective stocks via its disaster-response arm. The deployment continued a pattern of involvement the group has had in prior central-African Ebola responses.
nodes.disputed: Samaritan's Purse describes its deployments as filling acute clinical gaps in underserved zones; some Congolese civil-society voices describe foreign faith-based treatment centers as displacing local health workers and complicating community trust.

nodes.title: Responders warn of gaps and rising community distrust
nodes.what: Field organizations and WHO situation updates reported gaps in cold-chain capacity for rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine, irregular safe-burial team coverage, and incidents of resistance to contact tracing in several villages. Briefings flagged that response teams had been turned away or threatened in some communities. Coordinators tied the friction to memories of past outbreaks and broader mistrust of state and foreign actors.

nodes.title: Vaccination campaign scaled with Gavi-backed stockpile
nodes.what: Health authorities and partners expanded ring-vaccination using the rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine drawn from the global emergency stockpile coordinated by Gavi, WHO, UNICEF, and IFRC. Teams targeted frontline workers, contacts, and contacts-of-contacts in priority health zones. Implementers reported logistical strain in maintaining cold chain and reaching remote populations.

bands.label: Recurring eastern DRC outbreaks
bands.summary: Successive flare-ups in North Kivu and Ituri overlap with armed conflict, vaccine rollouts, and rising community distrust of health workers and camps.

nodes.title: DRC declares tenth Ebola outbreak in North Kivu
nodes.what: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's health ministry announced confirmed Ebola Zaire cases in Mangina, North Kivu, days after closing an unrelated outbreak in Equateur. The eastern setting placed the response in an active conflict zone for the first time, with armed groups operating around Beni and Butembo. Ring vaccination with the investigational rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine began within a week.

nodes.title: Treatment centers in Katwa and Butembo attacked
nodes.what: Armed assailants set fire to Ebola treatment centers run by Medecins Sans Frontieres in Katwa and Butembo within days of each other, forcing MSF to suspend operations in both towns. Responders described pervasive community distrust fueled by rumors and by the militarized escort posture around teams. The attacks coincided with a renewed rise in case counts across the affected health zones.
nodes.disputed: MSF described the attacks as evidence that the response had become too coercive and securitized to earn community trust; the DRC government and WHO described them as the work of organized spoilers exploiting local grievances rather than a verdict on the response model.

nodes.title: WHO declares PHEIC for Kivu outbreak
nodes.what: After a confirmed case reached Goma, a city of two million on the Rwandan border, the WHO Director-General accepted the Emergency Committee's recommendation to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. It was the fifth PHEIC declared since the 2005 International Health Regulations took effect. The committee stopped short of recommending border closures or travel restrictions.

nodes.title: Ervebo vaccine receives EMA marketing authorization
nodes.what: The European Medicines Agency granted conditional marketing authorization to Merck's Ervebo, the rVSV-ZEBOV-GP vaccine that had been used under research protocols throughout the Kivu outbreak. WHO prequalification followed days later, and the US FDA approved the vaccine in December. The decisions formalized a tool that had already been deployed to more than 250,000 people in eastern DRC.

nodes.title: Kivu outbreak declared over as Equateur flares again
nodes.what: DRC officials declared the North Kivu and Ituri epidemic ended after 2,287 deaths, the second largest Ebola outbreak on record. On the same arc a new outbreak was already underway in Equateur province in the country's northwest, eventually counting 130 cases and 55 deaths before its closure in November. Vaccine and rapid response teams were redeployed from the east.

nodes.title: Twelfth outbreak confirmed in North Kivu
nodes.what: Health authorities confirmed a new Ebola case in Butembo, North Kivu, in a woman whose husband had survived the earlier Kivu epidemic. Genomic sequencing linked the case to the 2018 to 2020 outbreak, raising questions about long-term viral persistence in survivors. The flare-up was contained at twelve cases by early May.

nodes.title: Uganda declares Sudan ebolavirus outbreak
nodes.what: Uganda's Ministry of Health confirmed a fatal case of Sudan ebolavirus in Mubende district, a species against which the licensed Ervebo vaccine is not effective. The outbreak spread to Kampala before being declared over in January 2023, with 142 confirmed cases and 55 confirmed deaths. The episode underscored that eastern Africa's Ebola risk was not limited to DRC's Zaire strain.

bands.label: Discovery and recurring flare-ups
bands.summary: Ebola is identified in 1976 near the Ebola River in northern Zaire, followed by intermittent outbreaks across central and west Africa and the slow build of regional response capacity.

nodes.title: Ebola identified near the Ebola River in northern Zaire
nodes.what: A hemorrhagic fever outbreak in and around Yambuku Mission Hospital in northern Zaire killed roughly 280 of 318 identified cases. Investigators traced spread through reused needles and close family contact, and named the new virus after the nearby Ebola River. A near-simultaneous outbreak in Nzara, Sudan was later attributed to a distinct species of the same virus.

nodes.title: Kikwit outbreak in Zaire
nodes.what: An outbreak centered on Kikwit General Hospital in Bandundu province sickened 315 people and killed 254. The event drew international teams from WHO and CDC and prompted new attention to nosocomial spread and barrier nursing in low-resource hospitals.

nodes.title: Gulu outbreak in Uganda
nodes.what: An outbreak of Ebola Sudan virus centered on Gulu, Masindi, and Mbarara districts produced 425 cases and 224 deaths over several months. Ugandan health authorities working with WHO used contact tracing and isolation wards to contain spread, and the response became a reference model for later African outbreaks.

nodes.title: West Africa epidemic declared
nodes.what: WHO and Guinean authorities confirmed Ebola in Guinea in March 2014, with spread soon documented in Liberia and Sierra Leone. The epidemic eventually produced more than 28,000 reported cases and over 11,000 deaths, the largest Ebola event on record, and exposed gaps in international outbreak response that drove later reform of WHO emergency capacity.
nodes.disputed: WHO describes the late escalation as a product of weak health systems and delayed alerts; MSF and several reviews describe it as a failure of the international response, including WHO itself, to act on early warnings.

nodes.title: Bas-Uele outbreak in DR Congo
nodes.what: DR Congo's health ministry and WHO confirmed an Ebola outbreak in Likati health zone, Bas-Uele province, producing eight cases and four deaths before containment. The response included the first field use of the rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine under a ring vaccination protocol agreed with Congolese authorities.
